assessment.nobel_worthiness: Transformative physiology-to-therapy arc: incretin biology explained postprandial insulin secretion and led to GLP-1 receptor agonists that now reshape treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and breadth of impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Decisive contributions are distributed: Holst on native GLP-1 physiology and secretion, Drucker on GLP-1 biology and the therapeutic rationale, Mojsov on identification of the active peptide form and synthesis. Knudsen led liraglutide/semaglutide development, but a three-person limit forces a choice between basic and industrial/translational credit; I favour the basic-discovery trio while acknowledging others (e.g. Habener, not on this list) are often cited.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation from large outcome trials and widespread clinical use; interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Exact allocation of credit among basic discoverers versus drug developers is contested and I have not independently verified who originated which finding.
Whether the prize should honour physiology or the drug development is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells redirected by chimeric antigen receptors established a new therapeutic modality, producing durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies. Conceptually original, clinically decisive and platform-defining for cell therapy.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed key CAR design (costimulation, CD28) and preclinical proof; June led the clinical translation and costimulatory-domain work leading to approved tisagenlecleucel. Rosenberg is credited for adoptive cell transfer and early clinical gene-engineered T cells but I place him outside a two-person configuration, since adoptive cell therapy overlaps with other candidate territory; early Eshhar/Gross CAR concepts are not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products, years of follow-up and independent confirmation; remaining questions about solid tumours and toxicity do not undermine the core achievement. Timely.
uncertainties: Credit for the original CAR concept versus clinical realisation is partly unresolved and persons outside the credited list may be relevant.
Long-term safety and secondary malignancy data are still maturing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of TOR and mTOR as the central controller linking nutrients and growth factors to cell growth, protein synthesis and metabolism; a unifying concept affecting cancer, diabetes, ageing and immunosuppression.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically in yeast and established its function in growth control; Sabatini identified mTOR in mammals and the nutrient-sensing pathway (Rag/GATOR, mTORC1/2 components). Schreiber contributed the FKBP12-rapamycin chemistry and mTOR binding, but the cleanest configuration is Hall plus Sabatini, though Brown/Sabatini mTOR identification credit is not fully clear from the list.
assessment.maturity: Findings widely replicated over three decades; the framework is mature and stable. Recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Whether a basic yeast discovery plus mammalian extension is better recognised with or without chemistry-based credit is a judgement call.
Other mammalian mTOR identifiers outside this list may deserve credit; I have not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Unfolded protein response is a fundamental homeostatic signalling pathway from ER to nucleus, with a clear mechanism (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing) and broad relevance to secretory physiology, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently and complementarily defined the pathway in yeast and mammals; this is a clean two-person attribution with long-recognised credit, though Ron/Harding on PERK arm are not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism well confirmed over decades; therapeutic translation is still partial but the basic discovery is mature and stable.
uncertainties: Translational impact is less established than for drug-backed candidates.
Contributions to PERK and ATF6 arms by others are not captured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishment of long-term culture of adult stem-cell-derived organoids has created a broadly used experimental platform for tissue biology, host-pathogen work and personalised disease modelling, built on Lgr5 stem-cell identification.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led identification of Lgr5 stem cells and the organoid culture system; Sato was the lead first author who developed the intestinal culture method. Two-person configuration is clean, though Wnt/Lgr5 work and other organoid pioneers (e.g. Sasai) lie outside this entry.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted and independently confirmed; clinical impact still developing, so maturity is moderate to good.
uncertainties: Whether the tool-like nature, rather than a mechanistic discovery, suits the prize.
Overlap with pluripotent-stem-cell organoid work not on this list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided a general method for causal control of defined cell populations with light, transforming neuroscience and enabling circuit-level dissection of behaviour and disease models; early clinical vision restoration trials exist.
assessment.attribution: Credit chain is long: Bamberg/Nagel/Hegemann characterised channelrhodopsin; Deisseroth and Boyden established neuronal use; Miesenböck contributed an earlier photosensitive-protein approach. Three-person cap forces exclusion of Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck, which is a real unfairness.
assessment.maturity: Method widely replicated and mature as a research tool; clinical translation is early.
uncertainties: Six credited names exceed a three-laureate prize; the allocation is highly contested.
Impact is chiefly as a research tool rather than direct therapy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and successors proved targeting a driver oncoprotein can convert a fatal leukemia into a chronic condition, establishing the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the drug discovery programme, Druker the clinical development and proof of concept, and Sawyers the resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors. Roles are complementary, and Rowley/Nowell and Witte's earlier BCR-ABL discovery work is not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Very mature with two decades of survival data; recognition is long established, arguably overdue though already widely honoured.
uncertainties: Prize guidance has traditionally favoured discoveries over drug development; fit uncertain.
Upstream discoverers of BCR-ABL are not among the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cytosolic DNA sensing through cGAS-cGAMP-STING defines a central innate immune pathway relevant to infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and ageing; a clear mechanistic discovery with substantial downstream drug development.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP as second messenger; Barber identified STING. Ishikawa shares STING credit, and Sun and Wu were Chen-lab first authors, but a Chen plus Barber configuration is the most defensible.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed but clinical translation is still early, so maturity is moderate and recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Competing claims on STING discovery (Ishikawa, Barber) and the role of trainees are not resolved.
Therapeutic translation has so far been limited.
